newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shanghai Coach mulling JV with Swedish fir.
newsitem.headline: China's Shanghai Coach mulling JV with Swedish fir.

text.p: Shanghai Coach Manufacturing Corp is considering starting a joint venture with a Swedish bus maker to make coaches for sale in China and abroad, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper did not identify the Swedish firm, but said Shanghai Coach was planning to expand its chassis and body production using imported technology.
"We aim to produce high-grade coaches for overseas and domestic markets," the newspaper quoted Lu Yuling, a manager with Shanghai Coach, as saying.
Japanese, French and German companies had also expressed interest in cooperation, Lu said but gave no further details.
Shanghai Coach, an arm of Chinese auto giant Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp (SAIC), will make about 1,700 coaches this year and planned to produce 3,000 vehicles a year by 2000, Lu said.
The bus market in the booming city of Shanghai is about 1,000 vehicles a year, accounting for about one-third of total demand in China, the newspaper said.
"China is a big coach market, with many buses to be replaced and many expressways under construction," Lu said.
Shanghai Coach's parent, SAIC, already has a big joint venture with German car maker Volkswagen AG and last week began work on a $1.57 billion venture with U.S. auto giant General Motors.
